about: Supply outlets, each: what one should carry. recommended_ls is the median of the makers' tested airflow where the outlet reaches about NC/NR 25 (quiet living rooms and bedrooms), most_ls the same at about NC/NR 30; one figure a maker. Ratings differ between makers (a US NC table allows 10 dB for the room, NR is a few points stricter), which is why the spread is wide. A linear slot is L/s a metre a slot. The neck velocity is on the nominal neck, at the recommendation.

rules.rule: With no maker's sound data, the neck at no more than 1.78 m/s for RC 25 and 2.16 m/s for RC 30, and lower where several outlets serve one room.
The flex run feeding an outlet carries no more than the flexible duct table's most for its size.
On a variable-airflow system, the final run to an outlet at no more than 3 m/s, to keep its noise down; the outlet maker's own data where it has it.
An outlet is sized for its throw, its face no faster than 700 fpm (3.56 m/s).
Floor grille boots: 300x100 on a 150, 300x100 on a 200, 350x150 on a 250, 300x150 on a 200 mm spigot; a 300x100 mainly for gas heating, its airflow being lower.
